Huntley College of Agriculture , Nutrition and Food Science Department Minor Required | Minor Electives | Notes | Program Website Minor Required: 11 units NTR 2030 - Health, Nutrition and the Integrated Being (3) or NTR 2050 - Personal and Consumer Nutrition (3) or NTR 2350 - Nutrition (3) or NTR 3050 - Nutrition, Science and Health (3) [GE 5D] NTR 3580 - Vegetarian and Plant Based Diets (2) NTR 3580A - Plant Based Meal Planning (1) NTR 3580L - Vegetarian and Plant Based Diets Lab (1) FST 3330 - Introduction to Plant Based Functional Foods (2) FST 3440 - Effect of Processing on Plant Based Foods (2) Minor Electives: 9 units Sustainability Electives: 3 units AG 2010 - Global Resources for Food (3) [GE 4A] BIO 3040 - Environment and Society (3) [GE 5D] GSC 1010 - Planet Earth: A Citizen’s Guide (2) and GSC 1010A - Planet Earth: A Citizen’s Guide Activity (1) PHL 4300 - Ethics, Environment, and Society (3) PLT 3650 - Sustainable Agriculture (2) and PLT 3650L - Sustainable Agriculture Laboratory (1) Other Electives: 6 units Select a minimum of 6 units from this list; at least one course must be upper division ABM 3130 - Food and Agriculture Policy (3) AG 2990 - Special Topics for Lower Division Students (1-3) AG 4010 - Ethical Issues in Food, Agricultural and Apparel Industries (3) [GE 3C or 4C] BIO 4590AS - Ethnobotany Service Learning Activity (2) and BIO 4590S - Ethnobotany - Service Learning (1) FST 3250 - Food Safety and Current Issues (3) [GE 5D] KIN 2070 - Health and Well-Being (3) NTR 1210 - Introduction to Foods (2) and NTR 1210L - Introduction to Foods Laboratory (1) NTR 3

courses.title: Health, Nutrition and the Integrated Being
courses.description: Investigation of specific areas of the integrated being dealing with nutrition, stress, drugs, sexuality, major health problems and death and dying. The integrated being and the development of behaviors and actions that will promote optimum physical and mental health will be investigated.

courses.title: Personal and Consumer Nutrition
courses.description: Improve knowledge and understanding of nutrition, nutrients, fitness and food safety related to health and wellness. Make healthy food choices based on MyPlate and other health recommendations. Consumer-decision making skills in meal planning, diet and exercise to aid in better diet, health and wellness.

courses.title: Nutrition
courses.description: For nutrition, dietetics, food science and technology majors, healthcare majors and physiology minors. Study of individual nutrient requirements. Utilization of dietary guidelines and other nutrition recommendations. Digestion, absorption, metabolism and excretion of macronutrients and micronutrients. Role of nutrition in health promotion, disease prevention and treatment of disease.
courses.prerequisites: Nutrition Major, Food Science and Technology Major, Nutrition Minor, or Physiology Minor.

courses.title: Nutrition, Science and Health
courses.description: [GE 5D] Integrative approach to nutrition, health, and fitness based on physiological and biochemical principles. Role of diet and other influences in promoting wellness and preventing degenerative diseases. Nutritional self-assessment project/weekly assignments/current controversies, submitted online typed discussions/assignments.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Vegetarian and Plant Based Diets
courses.description: Applications, research, theories, and health benefits of vegetarian and plant-based diets (PBDs). Includes discussion on food composition, benefits of PBDs, nutrition composition food categories and color. Diet modifications and alternatives to animal-based products are discussed. *The enforcement of this corequisite has been temporarily suspended in response to the switch to virtual and remote modes of instruction. Corequisite(s): NTR 3580L *.
courses.prerequisites: NTR 2030 , NTR 2050 , NTR 2350 / NTR 2350L , or NTR 3050 .

courses.title: Plant Based Meal Planning
courses.description: Cooking and processing of plant-based produce. Focus on menu development and meal planning for a plant based diet. Attention to nutrition, variety, and palatability will be reviewed for each menu. This course is designed to complement the material covered in the NTR 3580 . Pre or Corequisite(s): NTR 3580 / NTR 3580L .

courses.title: Vegetarian and Plant Based Diets Lab
courses.description: Cooking and processing of plant-based produce. Focus on cooking techniques that enhance flavor, palatability, texture, and nutrition. This course is designed to complement the material covered in the NTR 3580 lecture. *The enforcement of this corequisite has been temporarily suspended in response to the switch to virtual and remote modes of instruction. Corequisite(s): NTR 3580 *.
courses.prerequisites: NTR 2030 , NTR 2050 , NTR 2350 / NTR 2350L , or NTR 3050 .

courses.title: Introduction to Plant Based Functional Foods
courses.description: An introduction to functional foods and associated laws and regulations. Classification and chemistry of nutraceuticals and bioactive components in plant based functional foods and their health benefits. Factors involved in the development of new plant based functional foods.

courses.title: Effect of Processing on Plant Based Foods
courses.description: An introduction to different processing techniques such as thermal, nonthermal and others used by food industry to process food on large scale. Effect of processing on bioactive components. Use of processing techniques to produce new functional foods and protect bioactive components.

courses.title: Global Resources for Food
courses.description: [GE 4A] Examine the resource base for agricultural production on various continents, and whether there is potential for increasing food supplies. The role of agriculture in economic development will be addressed.

courses.title: Environment and Society
courses.description: [GE 5D] Environmental problems related to use of natural resources by modern societies. Issues discussed include availability of food, water, and energy by a rapidly growing world population, and the effects of pollution, climate change and decreasing biodiversity on ecosystems and societies. May be used as approved elective, but not for required upper division credit by students with majors in the Biological Sciences Department.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Planet Earth: A Citizen’s Guide
courses.description: Development of knowledge pertinent to Earth stewardship and global citizenship, with emphasis on building and maintaining a habitable earth. Survey of issues such as climate change, environmental and natural hazards, water resource development and conservation, and/or environmental sustainability, with their social, emotional, financial, psychological, and physiological impacts. Corequisite(s): GSC 1010A .

courses.title: Planet Earth: A Citizen’s Guide Activity
courses.description: Activities directed toward educating regional or campus communities about response to / recovery from challenges posed by Earth’s environment. Enhancement of skills to evaluate such challenges, engage in related conversations, and promote community awareness. Participation in events such as Earth Day, California Shake-Out, and disaster preparedness drills. Promotion of water conservation and waste recycling. Outdoor field trips. Corequisite(s): GSC 1010 .

courses.title: Ethics, Environment, and Society
courses.description: An examination of the moral and social philosophical aspects of the environmental crisis and the ecological movement.

courses.title: Sustainable Agriculture
courses.description: Current advances, issues and future directions in agriculture to ensure the long-term economic prosperity, environmental preservation, and social equity of food, fuel and fiber production. Corequisite(s): PLT 3650L .

courses.title: Sustainable Agriculture Laboratory
courses.description: Current advances, issues and future directions in agriculture to ensure the long-term economic prosperity, environmental preservation, and social equity of food, fuel and fiber production. Corequisite(s): PLT 3650 .

courses.title: Food and Agriculture Policy
courses.description: The political and historical framework affecting the food and agriculture system within the United States. Federal and state process of agricultural policy formation. Contemporary development and economic analysis of public programs and policies relating to agriculture, including: Food Safety, Nutrition, Trade, Conservation, and Farmer Supports. Current agricultural policies and programs as well as alternate policies evaluated. Evaluation of U.S. agricultural production and international trade policies and programs. Seminar discussions. Policy case studies.

courses.title: Special Topics for Lower Division Students
courses.description: Group study of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.title: Ethical Issues in Food, Agricultural and Apparel Industries
courses.description: [GE 3C or 4C] Socioeconomic and scientific issues in the Food, Agricultural, and Apparel Systems within a framework of moral philosophy and ethical reasoning. Analysis of topics in biotechnology in agricultural and apparel production, food processing, intellectual property rights, food safety, nutrition, the treatment of animals, the environment, labor rights in a global marketplace, and reducing world hunger and malnutrition.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Ethnobotany - Service Learning
courses.description: A community service-learning course that examines plant-human interactions in plant material culture, nutrition, foods as medicines, phytochemistry, and human uses of plant secondary metabolites. A focus is placed on local species. Practice ethnobotany skills during community-service ethnobotany-related activities for BioTrek. Corequisite(s): BIO 4590AS .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 121/BIO 121L, BIO 122/BIO 122L, and BIO 123/BIO 123L; BIO 121/BIO 121L and BIO 122/BIO 122L/BIO 1220C; BIO 121/BIO 121L/BIO 1210B and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L ; BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L ; BIO 115/115L/115A; or BIO 1150 / BIO 1150L .

courses.title: Food Safety and Current Issues
courses.description: [GE 5D] Overview of physical, chemical and microbiological hazards and their role in foodborne illness and the safety of the food supply. Introduction to the Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point System. The role of government and basic aspects of food safety laws and regulations. Review of current issues in food safety, food protection, food production, and food processing as they relate to public health.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Health and Well-Being
courses.description: Issues pertaining to stress management, mind/body health, interpersonal relationships, sexual health, fitness, nutrition, behavioral modification, and consumer health.

courses.title: Introduction to Foods
courses.description: Application and theory of food science concepts such as food composition, functional properties, and structure of foods. Study of food categories and basic culinary techniques. This course is required for: Dietetic majors, nutrition minors, and as an elective for Food Science majors. This course is required for: Dietetic majors, nutrition minors, and as an elective for Food Science majors. Corequisite(s): NTR 1210L .

courses.title: Introduction to Foods Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory application of food science concepts such as food composition, functional properties, and structure of foods. Study of food categories and basic culinary techniques. This course is required for: Dietetic majors, nutrition minors, and as an elective for Food Science majors. This course is required for: Dietetic majors, nutrition minors, and as an elective for Food Science majors. Corequisite(s): NTR 1210 .

courses.title: Food and Culture
courses.description: [GE 4C] Interrelationship of food availability, historical developments, socio-economic institutions, political, religious, and other influences on food patterns. In-depth study of a selected culture.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Food and Culture Laboratory
courses.description: Selected cultures, religious, traditional, medically modified cultural specialties, therapeutic modifications, countries and hands-on regional food preparation. Meal management according to culture preferences, and nutrient analysis software. Also, exploration of diverse worldviews as pertains relationships between food, history, culture and traditions. Individual oral reports and group projects.
courses.prerequisites: Nutrition Major, NTR 1210 or FN 121, and NTR 1210L or FN 121L. Pre or Corequisite(s): NTR 2280 or NTR 3280 .

courses.title: Farm-to-Table
courses.description: Cross Listed as: PLT 3860 Study of the farm-to-table movement. Focus in this course will be on small scale production, farmer’s markets and utilization of farm products. For nutrition, plant science, hospitality, and food science majors as well as plant-based nutrition and urban agriculture minors.

courses.title: Farm-to-Table
courses.description: Cross Listed as: NTR 3860 Study of the farm-to-table movement. Focus in this course will be on small scale production, farmer’s markets and utilization of farm products. For nutrition, plant science, hospitality, and food science majors as well as plant-based nutrition and urban agriculture minors.

courses.title: Subtropical Fruits
courses.description: Production of sub-tropical fruits and crops. Propagation, problem solving, harvesting, selection of best varieties and post-harvest technologies. Corequisite(s): PLT 2020L .

courses.title: Subtropical Fruits Laboratory
courses.description: Subtropical fruits, including date, olive, fig, macadamia, and other selected fruits for commercial planting. Climatic and cultural requirements, fruiting and growth habits, varietal characteristics. Corequisite(s): PLT 2020 .

courses.title: Culinary Produce Technology
courses.description: An integration of principles of culture, procurement, identification, and quality of both standard and gourmet vegetables, fruits, and herbs for restaurant and culinary uses. On site studies/discussion. Organic vs. standard produce. Case studies.

courses.title: Vegetable Crop Systems
courses.description: Cultural practices, varieties, economics of production of major warm and cool season vegetables. Application of production techniques on college operated acreage. Corequisite(s): PLT 2260L .

courses.title: Vegetable Crop Systems Laboratory
courses.description: Cultural practices, varieties, economics of production of major warm and cool season vegetables. Application of production techniques on college operated acreage, including Spadra farm. Corequisite(s): PLT 2260 .

courses.title: Plants and Civilization
courses.description: [GE 5D] A critical review of science, technology and environment as related to plant domestication and current world food, fiber, and fuel production. Societal implications associated with the biological and technical innovations in world cropping systems will be discussed. Open to all majors. Open to all majors.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.
